content.text: {"headline":"Approve P1: shift breaks and extend IVR callback on both queues. It costs nothing and is predicted to lift service level to 93.9% for 13:45-15:45, against an 80% target.","why":"Payments is short-staffed because of a sick wave: 7 absences against a usual 2.6, 4 noted as dengue. At 13:30 there were 19 agents on the phones against 32 planned, while calls ran 9% under forecast. Doing nothing (P0) is predicted to just scrape the target at 83.7%, with payments at 81.2% and handle time running above forecast (e.g. 341s vs 287s at 13:00). That leaves little margin. P1 delays the 14:45-15:15 breaks (payments by 45 min, general by 30 min) and adds IVR callback on both queues from 15:00 to 16:00. It is predicted to bring payments to 93.7% and general to 94.3%, cut abandons from 3.0% to 1.2%, and raise the rest-of-day figure to 96.7%. There is no extra cost and no policy issues.","trade_offs":["P0 costs nothing but is only predicted to reach 83.7%, and payments at 81.2% is barely above target. Any further absence or handle-time creep could tip it under.","P2 (INR 882) adds only 1.5 points (95.4%) by cancelling payments coaching and deflecting some enquiries to chat. It is not needed to hit the target.","P3 (INR 1,551) and P4 (INR 2,952, with overtime for 13 agents) reach 96.0% and 98.1%, with abandons down to 0.7% and 0.4%. These are small customer gains for real spend.","P1 delays general's breaks by 30 min to protect the shared load, so general agents also give up some timing flexibility. Its predicted service level still improves, from 87.0% to 94.3%."],"watch":"Watch payments agents on the phones against plan, and any new sick calls. The 7 absences don't explain the full 13-agent gap, so other unplanned off-phone time may be adding to it. Also watch handle time. If payments service level drifts toward 80% before 15:00, step up to P2 (INR 882) by cancelling payments coaching and adding chat deflection."}
